name: Research Labs

orgs.name: Allen Institute for AI
orgs.note: Ai2 (the Allen Institute for AI) describes itself as a non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by Paul G. Allen; source URL verified 2026-08-14

blurb:
The organisations doing frontier AI research, grouped by what funds them rather than by reputation. Commercial labs answer to shareholders, university labs to funding bodies and peer review, and government labs to a national programme. That distinction shapes what each publishes and what each keeps.

Three regions anchor the field and each is strong in different things. The United States leads in private venture capital, frontier model breakthroughs, and hardware and software co-design. China leads in publication volume, open-weights releases, computer vision, and the speed of industrial deployment. Europe concentrates on open-weights models, safety research, industrial automation, and academic networks that span borders rather than sitting in one institution.

No count of AI research labs is authoritative, because the category runs from multi-billion-dollar corporate divisions to a university department with four people. Industry databases index well over a thousand commercial labs. The US National Science Foundation alone funds 29 National AI Research Institutes connecting more than 500 institutions, and global mapping efforts count over a hundred government-backed AI safety institutes.

What this page tracks is narrower and verifiable: labs this site holds a sourced profile for, each with its own page, its headquarters as its own site states it, and whatever else we track about it. The list grows as profiles are written, and it is not a ranking.

reading.body:
Research labs are organizational units conducting frontier or industrial AI work, though this data covers only one entity and thus cannot characterize the category's scale or diversity.

The Allen Institute for AI stands as a non-profit model for AI research, distinct from the venture-backed and corporate labs that dominate frontier development. Its founding in 2014 by a technology billionaire represents one path to sustained research capacity outside traditional academic and industry structures. The institute's self-description emphasizes independence, though the data does not specify its funding sources beyond the founding relationship, its annual operating budget, or whether it operates specialized computing facilities.

This entry documents organizational form rather than capabilities, infrastructure, or output. It does not reveal how research labs relate to the compute, buildings, or power systems that constrain AI scaling. Whether non-profit labs operate their own data centers, purchase capacity from cloud providers, or depend on university infrastructure remains outside the scope here. The single example also cannot show whether non-profit research institutions represent a growing or shrinking share of frontier AI work.
